Read the draft paragraph.

(1) Last spring, the fourth graders at Maple Elementary planted a vegetable garden behind the gym. (2) Each class took care of one raised bed. (3) The students measured the beds, chose the seeds, and kept a daily watering chart. (4) The school cafeteria was built in 1985. (5) Most of the plants grew well. (6) ___, the tomatoes in one bed wilted because they did not get enough water. (7) The project was a success. (8) Teachers plan to repeat it next year.

Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?
choices: Sentence 4
Sentence 5
Sentence 6
Sentence 7
Sentence 8
oneLineConcept: Remove a sentence that does not support the paragraph's main point.
explanation:
The paragraph is about the students' garden project. When the cafeteria was built has nothing to do with the garden, so sentence 4 should be removed.

**Wrong choices**
- "Sentence 5": Sentence 5 reports how the garden grew, which is on topic.
- "Sentence 6": Sentence 6 gives a problem the students had with the garden.
- "Sentence 7": Sentence 7 sums up the project.
- "Sentence 8": Sentence 8 tells what will happen next, which closes the paragraph.

(3) The students measured the beds, chose the seeds, and kept a daily watering chart. (4) The school cafeteria was built in 1985. (5) Most of the plants grew well. (6) ___, the tomatoes in one bed wilted because they did not get enough water. (7) The project was a success. (8) Teachers plan to repeat it next year.

Which word or phrase best fills the blank at the start of sentence 6?
choices: Therefore,
For example,
Similarly,
However,
As a result,
oneLineConcept: A transition must match the relationship between the ideas.
explanation:
Sentence 5 says most plants grew well; sentence 6 describes plants that did not. That is a contrast, so "However" is the right transition.

**Wrong choices**
- "Therefore,": "Therefore" shows a result, but wilting is not a result of plants growing well.
- "For example,": "For example" would introduce an example of plants growing well.
- "Similarly,": "Similarly" shows likeness, but the ideas are opposite.
- "As a result,": "As a result" shows cause and effect, which does not fit.

Read the draft paragraph.

(1) Last spring, the fourth graders at Maple Elementary planted a vegetable garden behind the gym. (2) Each class took care of one raised bed. (3) The students measured the beds, chose the seeds, and kept a daily watering chart. (4) The school cafeteria was built in 1985. (5) Most of the plants grew well. (6) ___, the tomatoes in one bed wilted because they did not get enough water. (7) The project was a success. (8) Teachers plan to repeat it next year.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 7 and 8?
choices: The project was a success, teachers plan to repeat it next year.
The project was a success, so teachers plan to repeat it next year.
The project was a success, although teachers plan to repeat it next year.
Being a success, teachers plan to repeat the project next year.
The project, which teachers plan to repeat next year because it was a success.
oneLineConcept: Combine sentences with a word that shows the real relationship.
explanation:
The teachers want to repeat the project because it succeeded. A comma plus "so" joins the two complete sentences and shows cause and effect.

**Wrong choices**
- "The project was a success, teachers plan to repeat it next year.": Two complete sentences joined only by a comma form a comma splice.
- "The project was a success, although teachers plan to repeat it next year.": "Although" shows contrast, but there is no contrast here.
- "Being a success, teachers plan to repeat the project next year.": This says the teachers were a success (a dangling modifier).
- "The project, which teachers plan to repeat next year because it was a success.": This has no main verb, so it is a fragment.

stem:
Read the draft of a letter to a city council.

(1) The Riverside Public Library is asking the city council to restore its Sunday hours. (2) Until last year, the library was open from noon to 5 p.m. on Sundays. (3) Many working parents used those hours to bring their children to story time. (4) Students also depended on the library's free computers to finish homework. (5) Cutting Sunday hours was a totally dumb move by the council. (6) Restoring the hours would cost about the same as the library's yearly budget for new magazines. (7) ___

Which revision of sentence 5 best fits the tone of the letter?
choices: Cutting Sunday hours was a really bad idea, to be honest.
The council messed up big time when it cut Sunday hours.
Anyone can see that cutting Sunday hours was foolish.
Who in their right mind would cut Sunday hours?
Cutting Sunday hours made it harder for these families and students to use the library.
oneLineConcept: Keep the tone and style of the rest of the passage.
explanation:
The letter is formal and polite, and it supports its request with facts. The best revision explains the effect of the cut without insulting the council.

**Wrong choices**
- "Cutting Sunday hours was a really bad idea, to be honest.": "Really bad idea, to be honest" is too casual for a formal letter.
- "The council messed up big time when it cut Sunday hours.": "Messed up big time" is slang.
- "Anyone can see that cutting Sunday hours was foolish.": Calling the decision "foolish" insults the readers the letter is trying to persuade.
- "Who in their right mind would cut Sunday hours?": A sarcastic question is rude and does not give a reason.

Read the draft of a letter to a city council.

(1) The Riverside Public Library is asking the city council to restore its Sunday hours. (2) Until last year, the library was open from noon to 5 p.m. on Sundays. (3) Many working parents used those hours to bring their children to story time. (4) Students also depended on the library's free computers to finish homework. (5) Cutting Sunday hours was a totally dumb move by the council. (6) Restoring the hours would cost about the same as the library's yearly budget for new magazines. (7) ___

Which sentence would best fill blank (7) as the conclusion of the letter?
choices: The library also has a large collection of mystery novels.
Some people prefer to read e-books at home.
For these reasons, we ask the council to restore Sunday hours in next year's budget.
Story time is usually held in the children's room.
The library was first built many years ago.
oneLineConcept: A conclusion should restate the main point of the passage.
explanation:
The letter's purpose, stated in sentence 1, is to ask for Sunday hours to return. A good conclusion repeats that request and ties it to the reasons given.

**Wrong choices**
- "The library also has a large collection of mystery novels.": The mystery collection is a new detail that does not support the request.
- "Some people prefer to read e-books at home.": This works against the letter's argument and does not conclude it.
- "Story time is usually held in the children's room.": This is a minor detail, not a conclusion.
- "The library was first built many years ago.": The library's age is unrelated to the request.

The writer wants to add this sentence: "For many of them, Sunday was the only day they were not at work." Where would it best fit?
choices: After sentence 1
After sentence 2
After sentence 3
After sentence 4
After sentence 6
oneLineConcept: An added sentence must sit next to the idea it explains.
explanation:
The new sentence explains why "working parents" needed Sunday hours, and "them" must point back to those parents. That only works right after sentence 3.

**Wrong choices**
- "After sentence 1": After sentence 1 there are no people for "them" to refer to.
- "After sentence 2": After sentence 2, "them" would have no clear reference.
- "After sentence 4": After sentence 4, "them" would refer to the students, who are not described as working.
- "After sentence 6": After sentence 6, the sentence would interrupt the move to the conclusion and "them" would be unclear.

stem:
Read the draft paragraph from a student essay.

(1) Many teenagers do not get enough sleep on school nights. (2) Sleep experts recommend that teenagers sleep eight to ten hours a night. (3) However, a survey at our school found that most students sleep fewer than seven hours. (4) Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class. (5) It can also affect mood and memory. (6) Some schools have responded by starting classes later in the morning. (7) My cousin's school has a large swimming pool. (8) Our school board should consider doing the same.

Which sentence should be deleted to improve the focus of the paragraph?
choices: Sentence 2
Sentence 4
Sentence 6
Sentence 7
Sentence 8
oneLineConcept: Delete details that do not relate to the paragraph's topic.
explanation:
The paragraph is about teenagers' sleep and later school start times. A swimming pool has nothing to do with sleep, and it also separates sentence 8 from the idea it refers to.

**Wrong choices**
- "Sentence 2": Sentence 2 gives the recommended amount of sleep, which supports the topic.
- "Sentence 4": Sentence 4 explains a problem caused by lack of sleep.
- "Sentence 6": Sentence 6 introduces the solution the paragraph recommends.
- "Sentence 8": Sentence 8 gives the writer's recommendation, the paragraph's goal.

Read the draft paragraph from a student essay.

(1) Many teenagers do not get enough sleep on school nights. (2) Sleep experts recommend that teenagers sleep eight to ten hours a night. (3) However, a survey at our school found that most students sleep fewer than seven hours. (4) Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class. (5) It can also affect mood and memory. (6) Some schools have responded by starting classes later in the morning. (7) My cousin's school has a large swimming pool. (8) Our school board should consider doing the same.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 4 and 5?
choices: Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class and can also affect mood and memory.
Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class, it can also affect mood and memory.
Lack of sleep, which can make it hard to pay attention in class and also affect mood and memory.
Although lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class, it can also affect mood and memory.
Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class; and it can also affect mood and memory.
oneLineConcept: Sentences with the same subject can share it through a compound verb.
explanation:
Both sentences have the same subject (lack of sleep), so they can share it: "can make ... and can also affect." The result is correct and concise.

**Wrong choices**
- "Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class, it can also affect mood and memory.": This is a comma splice.
- "Lack of sleep, which can make it hard to pay attention in class and also affect mood and memory.": This has no main verb, so it is a fragment.
- "Although lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class, it can also affect mood and memory.": "Although" shows contrast, but both ideas are harmful effects.
- "Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class; and it can also affect mood and memory.": A semicolon should not be followed by "and" when joining two simple sentences like these.

stem:
Read the draft paragraph from a student essay.

(1) Many teenagers do not get enough sleep on school nights. (2) Sleep experts recommend that teenagers sleep eight to ten hours a night. (3) However, a survey at our school found that most students sleep fewer than seven hours. (4) Lack of sleep can make it hard to pay attention in class. (5) It can also affect mood and memory. (6) Some schools have responded by starting classes later in the morning. (7) My cousin's school has a large swimming pool. (8) Our school board should consider doing the same.

The writer wants to add a sentence after sentence 6 to explain why later start times might help. Which sentence does this best?
choices: Some students prefer to study late at night with their friends.
Many schools also serve breakfast before classes begin.
Starting classes later is the only way to solve every problem in schools.
School buses are expensive to run in some districts.
A later start lets students sleep longer in the morning, closer to the amount experts recommend.
oneLineConcept: Added support must explain the point directly and not overstate it.
explanation:
The paragraph argues that a later start can help students who lack sleep. The best sentence links the later start to more sleep and to the recommendation in sentence 2.

**Wrong choices**
- "Some students prefer to study late at night with their friends.": Studying late with friends does not explain how later start times help.
- "Many schools also serve breakfast before classes begin.": Breakfast is a different topic.
- "Starting classes later is the only way to solve every problem in schools.": "The only way to solve every problem" is an overstatement the paragraph cannot support.
- "School buses are expensive to run in some districts.": Bus costs are off topic and do not explain the benefit.
